Document: Practice Direction 51R – Online Civil Money Claims Pilot
Part 5 of 10
==================================================
[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.8(1) If –] Claimant accepts the defendant’s proposed repayment plan, proposes a settlement agreement, instead of requesting a judgment on admission – defendant rejects the proposal for a settlement agreement, or does not respond

## 7.9(1) If –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (a)  instead of requesting a judgment on admission, the claimant has proposed a settlement agreement on the same terms as the defendant’s proposed repayment plan;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (za) none of the parties is represented by a legal representative;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (b) the proposed agreement is in the form of OCON Settlement Agreement A;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (c) the claimant has used the OCMC website to notify the court of the proposal to the defendant; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (d) the defendant has, within 7 days of the date of the claimant’s proposal, used the OCMC website to notify the court that they have rejected the proposal and do not agree to the settlement agreement, or within that time has failed to notify the court of their response, the claimant may request a judgment on admission. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (2) The claimant requests a judgment on admission by completing form OCON225 and submitting it to the court using the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (3) If the court receives a request for judgment on admission, it must “enter judgment” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (4) The judgment will be made for the amount of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (a) the claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (b) any interest that the claimant is entitled to and has claimed on the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (c) court fees,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] minus any payments of the amount owed on the claim form that the defendant has already paid. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (If a claimant wants to claim any costs other than court fees, for example the costs of paying for expert evidence, the claimant would have to make an application. Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (5) The judgment must state that the amount is to be paid in accordance with the defendant’s proposed repayment plan, unless, at the time the judgment is made, a repayment date specified in the repayment plan has passed. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (6) If a repayment date specified in the defendant’s repayment plan has passed before the judgment is made, the judgment must still be made in accordance with that repayment plan, but –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (a) if the repayment plan states that the whole of the amount owed is to be paid by a date that has passed, the judgment must state that repayment must be made immediately;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (b) if the repayment plan states that the amount owed is to be paid by instalments and the date of the first instalment has passed, the judgment must state that the first instalment must be made by a date that is one calendar month after the date of the judgment, and with subsequent instalments to be paid at one calendar month intervals after that. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] Claimant rejects the defendant’s proposed repayment plan, proposes different plan; defendant is an individual, which includes a sole trader; affordability calculation

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] 7.10(1) Subject to paragraph (2A), this paragraph, and paragraphs 7.11 to 7.15 apply where the defendant is an individual, which includes a sole trader, and the claimant is not represented by a legal representative. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (2) If the claimant has rejected the defendant’s proposed repayment plan, the claimant may also suggest a repayment plan. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (2A) Paragraph (2)also applies where the claimant is or all the parties are, represented by a legal representative, and in such a case, on receiving the claimant’s suggested repayment plan, the court will send the case out of Online Civil Money Claims, to the CTSC (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (3) On receiving the claimant’s suggested repayment plan, the court will produce an “affordability calculation”. The affordability calculation will be carried out electronically, by the application of a formula to the information submitted by the parties. The purpose of the calculation is to establish what rate of repayment a defendant is likely to be able to afford, based on the information submitted by the parties: an “affordability calculation repayment plan”. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (4) The explanation of the formula is set out in Annex A to this practice direction. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (5) If the affordability calculation indicates that the defendant will not be able to afford to repay the amount owed in accordance with the claimant’s repayment plan, the court will tell the claimant, and ask the claimant whether they accept or reject the affordability calculation repayment plan instead. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (6) The claimant may accept or reject the affordability calculation repayment plan using the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] Claimant accepts affordability calculation repayment plan, or that plan amounts to the claimant’s proposed repayment plan – court asks claimant whether they request judgment, or are proposing a settlement agreement instead

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] 7.11 If the claimant accepts the affordability calculation repayment plan, or if that plan is calculated as amounting to the claimant’s repayment plan, the court will ask the claimant whether they wish to request judgment on admission, or whether they are proposing a settlement agreement instead. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] Claimant accepts affordability calculation repayment plan or that plan amounts to the claimant’s proposed repayment plan – claimant requests judgment

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] 7.12(1) If, after an affordability calculation has been done and the court has asked the claimant how they wish to proceed, the claimant wishes to request a judgment on admission, they may make the request by completing form OCON225A and submitting it to the court using the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (2) If the court receives a request for judgment, it must “enter judgment” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (3) The judgment will be made for the amount of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (a) the claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (b) any interest that the claimant is entitled to and has claimed on the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (c) court fees,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] minus any payments of the amount owed on the claim form that the defendant has already paid. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (If a claimant wants to claim any costs other than court fees, for example the costs of paying for expert evidence, the claimant would have to make an application. Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (4) The judgment must state that the amount is to be paid in accordance with the affordability calculation repayment plan (as defined), unless, at the time the judgment is made, a repayment date specified in the affordability calculation repayment plan has passed. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (4A) If a repayment date specified in the affordability calculation repayment plan has passed before the judgment is made, the judgment must still be made in accordance with that repayment plan, but –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (a) if the repayment plan states that the whole of the amount owed is to be paid by a date that has passed, the judgment must state that repayment must be made immediately;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (b) if the repayment plan states that the amount owed is to be paid by instalments and the date of the first instalment has passed, the judgment must state that the first instalment must be made by a date that is one calendar month after the date of the judgment, and with subsequent instalments to be paid at one calendar month intervals after that. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (5) If, after judgment has been made, the defendant objects to the affordability calculation repayment plan, or if the claimant no longer agrees to the plan, they may ask, on time, for a redetermination by a judge of the plan for the repayment of the amount owed by the defendant. The claimant or defendant may make their request for redetermination to the court by email to the OCMC email address, or on paper to the OCMC postal address (as defined). When requesting a redetermination, the claimant or defendant must explain why they object to the affordability calculation repayment plan. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (6) The request for redetermination will be submitted to the court on time if it is received by the court within 19 days after the date of the judgment. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (7) If the court receives a request for redetermination on time, it must send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims to the defendant’s “home court” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] Following affordability calculation, claimant proposes settlement agreement, and defendant accepts the settlement agreement

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] 7.13(1) This paragraph applies, if, after an affordability calculation has been done and the court has asked the claimant how they wish to proceed –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (a)  the claimant uses the OCMC website to tell the court that –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (i) it proposes a settlement agreement to the defendant;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (ii) the settlement agreement is in the form of OCON Settlement Agreement A; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (iii) the settlement agreement is for repayment of the amount owed in accordance with the affordability calculation repayment plan, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (b) the defendant has, within 7 days of the date of the claimant’s proposal, used the OCMC website to notify the court that they have accepted the proposal and agree to the settlement agreement. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (2) If the defendant has accepted the settlement agreement in those circumstances, the court must “stay” the proceedings (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (3) When it stays the proceedings, the court must enable the claimant to return to court to request judgment on admission for any money still owed under the settlement agreement, if the settlement agreement breaks down and the defendant fails to comply with the settlement agreement. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (4) If the settlement agreement breaks down, the claimant requests judgment on admission by completing form OCON225 and submitting it to the court using the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (5) If the court receives a request for judgment on admission, it must “enter judgment” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (6) The judgment will be made for the amount of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (a) the claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (b) any interest that the claimant is entitled to and has claimed on the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (c) court fees,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] minus any payments of the amount owed on the claim form that the defendant has already paid. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (If a claimant wants to claim any costs other than court fees, for example the costs of paying for expert evidence, the claimant would have to make an application. Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (7) The judgment must state that the amount is to be paid in accordance with the terms of the settlement agreement, unless, at the time the judgment is made, a repayment date specified in the settlement agreement has passed. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (8) If a repayment date specified in the settlement agreement has passed before the judgment is made, the judgment must still be made in accordance with that settlement agreement, but –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (a) if the settlement agreement states that the whole of the amount owed is to be paid by a date that has passed, the judgment must state that repayment must be made immediately;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (b) if the settlement agreement states that the amount owed is to be paid by instalments and the date of the first instalment has passed, the judgment must state that the first instalment must be made by a date that is one calendar month after the date of the judgment, and with subsequent instalments to be paid at one calendar month intervals after that. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] Following affordability calculation, claimant proposes settlement agreement, but defendant rejects the settlement agreement, or fails to respond

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] 7.14(1) This paragraph applies, if, after an affordability calculation has been done and the court has asked the claimant how they wish to proceed –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (a) the claimant uses the OCMC website to tell the court that –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (i) it proposes a settlement agreement to the defendant;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (ii) the settlement agreement is in the form of OCON Settlement Agreement A; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (iii) the settlement agreement is for repayment of the amount owed in accordance with the affordability calculation repayment plan; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (b) within 7 days of the date of the claimant’s proposal, the defendant uses the OCMC website to tell the court that they reject the settlement agreement or the defendant does not respond to the court within the 7 days. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (2) If the defendant has rejected the settlement agreement or failed to respond within the 7 days in those circumstances, the claimant can request judgment on admission, by completing form OCON225 and submitting it to the court using the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (3) If the court receives a request for judgment on admission, it must “enter judgment” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (4) The judgment will be made for the amount of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (a) the claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (b) any interest that the claimant is entitled to and has claimed on the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (c) court fees,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] minus any payments of the amount owed on the claim form that the defendant has already paid. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (If a claimant wants to claim any costs other than court fees, for example the costs of paying for expert evidence, the claimant would have to make an application. Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (5) The judgment must state that the amount is to be paid in accordance with the affordability calculation repayment plan, unless, at the time the judgment is made, a repayment date specified in the affordability calculation repayment plan has passed. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (5A) If a repayment date specified in the affordability calculation repayment plan has passed before the judgment is made, the judgment must still be made in accordance with that repayment plan, but –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (a) if the repayment plan states that the whole of the amount owed is to be paid by a date that has passed, the judgment must state that repayment must be made immediately;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (b) if the repayment plan states that the amount owed is to be paid by instalments and the date of the first instalment has passed, the judgment must state that the first instalment must be made by a date that is one calendar month after the date of the judgment, and with subsequent instalments to be paid at one calendar month intervals after that. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (6) If, after the judgment has been made, the claimant changes their mind about the affordability calculation repayment plan and wishes to object to the plan, or the defendant wishes to object to the affordability calculation repayment plan, they may ask, on time, for a redetermination by a judge of the plan for the repayment of the amount owed by the defendant. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (7) The claimant or defendant may make their request for redetermination to the court by email to the OCMC email address, or on paper to the OCMC postal address (as defined). When requesting a redetermination, the claimant or defendant must explain why they object to the affordability calculation repayment plan. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (8) The request for redetermination will be submitted to the court on time if it is received by the court within 19 days after the date of the judgment. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (9) If the court receives a request for redetermination on time, it must send the claim out of OCMC to the defendant’s “home court” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] Claimant rejects defendant’s proposed repayment plan, and also rejects affordability calculation repayment plan – judgment with repayment plan to be determined

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] 7.15(1) If, following an affordability calculation, the claimant wishes to reject the affordability calculation repayment plan, they may do so using the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (2) If the claimant rejects the affordability calculation repayment plan, they may still request judgment on admission, by completing form OCON225 and submitting it to the court using the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (3) If the court receives a request for judgment on admission, it must “enter judgment” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (4) The judgment will be made for the amount of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (a) the claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (b) any interest that the claimant is entitled to and has claimed on the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (c) court fees,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] minus any payments of the amount owed on the claim form that the defendant has already paid. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (If a claimant wants to claim any costs other than court fees, for example the costs of paying for expert evidence, the claimant would have to make an application. Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (5) The judgment must state that the plan for the repayment of the amount owed by the defendant is to be determined. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (6) The plan for the repayment of the amount owed by the defendant must be ordered by a judge. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (7) If either party objects to the plan for repayment ordered by the judge, they may ask, on time, for a redetermination of the plan for the repayment of the amount owed by the defendant. The claimant or defendant may make their request for redetermination to the court by email to the OCMC email address, or on paper to the OCMC postal address (as defined). When requesting a redetermination, the claimant or defendant must explain why they object to the plan ordered by the judge. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (8) The request for redetermination will be submitted to the court on time if it is received by the court within 19 days after the date of the judgment. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] (9) If the court receives a request for redetermination on time, it must send the claim out of OCMC to the defendant’s “home court” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.9(1) If –] Claimant rejects the defendant’s proposed repayment plan, proposes different terms – defendant is not an individual

## 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –] (a) the defendant is not an individual; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –] (b) the claimant has rejected the defendant’s proposed repayment plan. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –] (2) The claimant may also suggest a repayment plan. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –] (3) On receiving the claimant’s rejection, the court will send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims, to the “CNBC” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –] Claimant fails to respond to defendant’s proposed repayment plan, or to the affordability calculation repayment plan

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –] 7.17 If, within 33 days after being asked by the court, the claimant fails to tell the court whether they accept –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –] (a)  the defendant’s proposed repayment plan; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –] (b) (where relevant) the affordability calculation repayment plan,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –] the court must “stay” the proceedings (as defined). If the claimant then responds later, the court must automatically “lift” the stay (as defined) to allow the proceedings to be resumed. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –] Sections 7.18 to 7.36 – Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –] Sub-section D – Part admission and defence of the rest of the claim

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –] When this sub-section applies

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –] 7.37 This sub-section applies where the defendant part admits the claim and defends the rest of the claim and uses the response screens on the OCMC website to make the part admission and part defence. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –] Court to notify the claimant where the defendant proposes to make payment of the partial amount admitted, and that the defendant is also defending the rest of the claim

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –] 7.38 When the court tells the claimant that it has received the part admission, it must also tell the claimant –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –] (a) whether the defendant has offered to pay the whole amount admitted so that the claimant received it within 5 days of the date of the admission, or whether the defendant has asked for more time to pay;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –] (b) if the defendant has asked for more time to pay, what “repayment plan” (as defined) the defendant is proposing for payment which could be payment so that the claimant received it by a date that is more than 5 days after the date of part admission, or payment by instalments; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –] (c) that the defendant is defending the rest of the claim. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.16(1) This paragraph applies where –] Court to send case out of Online Civil Money Claims following notification to the claimant made pursuant to paragraph 7.38 in certain circumstances

## 7.38A Where—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.38A Where—] (a) the court has made a notification to the claimant pursuant to paragraph 7.38; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.38A Where—] (b) the defendant (but not the claimant) is represented by a legal representative,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.38A Where—] the claim must be sent out of Online Civil Money Claims to the CTSC (as defined) at that stage.
